items.title: George "Happy" Schilling Interview, 1957-09-08
items.q: I had a job at Smith's Cottage one Sunday, and I wanted to get musicians together. I don't know what happened, but then I got a hold of Dave Pertons on valve trombone, Archie on clarinet, and Baptiste on quine on fiddle, and me, and Harry Shannon, and Rag Baby Stevens

ctx.x: I think you're playing see the third line, I mean the third space, and it sounds the first line. But George used to play an awful lot of picnics, didn't you?

Oh, yeah. Most of your work was picnics, wasn't it? In those days, New Orleans used to give a terrible lot of picnics, didn't they? That was all the rage for a time, wasn't it? Out at Nuremberg on a Sunday, if they didn't have 25 or 30 bands, they didn't have two. And out at West End, too? All over the places. West End, they had two places at West End. One of them was Brunnings, Pavilion. They have all their things. If they had a dollar and a half a couple to go there, and they give you a chicken and spaghetti…
Yeah, Papa Lane, though, he played with him, too.
